item.title: Re: Locations
item.content:encoded:
But "North America" isn't a country, it's a continent. I was thinking it might be something like Sierra Leone or South Africa, though they're not particularly good fits for the relative lengths. Maybe even United Kingdom…

Also if you think of the blocks as being equivalent to text redacted on a photocopied document using a black marker (or removable tape, if you're making a redacted copy of an original you don't want to permanently alter), it doesn't necessarily hold that number_of_blocks == number_of_letters, when displayed in a variable-width font. It's fairly consistent for numbers, but not text. So it could be roughly but not necessarily exactly five letters followed by seven, merely combinations that add up to about the same physical width.

Plus of course the author might have just shoved them in at random without thinking of any one place in particular.

item.title: Staff Post
item.content:encoded:
"Can I write cross testing?" Let's find out! Hm, checking the FAQ…

Can I cross-test? Can I use crosslinks?

Yes. Please read the Crosslinks guide in How To Write An SCP first.

Oh! I see! So what does that guide say?

…well now. It says quite a bit on the subject of crosslinking! It's got a whole tab dedicated to it. But let's focus just on the cross testing itself…

In short, there are three major views:

One major view of the Foundation holds that we do not cross-test SCPs. Ever.
Another major view of the Foundation holds that we do, in fact, cross-test SCPs.
A third major view of the Foundation takes a middle road. Maybe some Sites cross-test SCPs, and others forbid all cross-testing.
Which view is correct? Well, that depends on you, and your story. Choose with care.

Or, in other words, this is a matter of the writer's headcanon, and not something we are restricting.

Nanoro, you are free to express your view that crosstesting is a Bad Idea(TM), and many would agree with you on it. But please refrain from directly advising other users that it is something we don't do at all or "anymore", as this is not true.

Thank you.

item.title: Re: Potential Cross Test?
item.content:encoded: Cross-testing isn't really a thing we do anymore, mostly due to it usually being pretty pointless and quite frankly dumb. I mean, if you mix two anomalous objects, there's no telling what'll happen. If either has some property that doesn't match well with the other, the results can easily spin out of control - hell, at best we get mass destruction and at worst we get more things to contain. So yeah, crosstesting is a Bad Idea (TM).

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Wait, where do I say that they "enter" sleep? They hunt by disabling the victim's ability to sleep, sometimes causing hallucinations, and that's pretty much it.

I have ideas for those, but SCP articles are meant to be shorter and to the point, so I don't really think I'll be writing more about them for the site.

A quick rundown for their general behaviour, if you're curious:
A quick rundown for their general behaviour, if you're curious:

They live alone for most of the year, seasonally forming pairs for mating. The pair will remain together until the end of their mating season, regardless of whether or not the female gives birth. They don't raise their children, as they're born auto-sufficient and will flee the nest as soon as they can walk. Children look like smaller versions of the adults, and hunt small animals such as mice, cats and dogs, hunting larger game like sheep, humans and cows only after reaching adulthood.

Although they usually prefer to live and hunt only individually or in mated pairs, they are extremely tolerant of other members of their species, and will share territory and meals with no problem. Intraspecies violence is almost entirely unheard of, occuring only during times of extreme stress. MTF teams hunting them report occasions where a group will act together in a strangely coordinated fashion in order to avoid capture/death, succeeding more than 90% of the time. It also seems that ever since the Foundation started hunting them, the amount of individuals sharing the same territory increased, being normal to find 5 to 10 individuals in the same general area.

Thanks for the upvote!
